title: Signal standardization and smart oncall throttler for SLO reduction windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our current SLO evaluation and alerting stack is brittle because traces, metrics, and logs arrive with inconsistent tags and sampling headers. This leads to noisy burn-rate pages during routine infra work and uneven SLO computation for model-serving routes (text-gen vs embeddings). Goal: Build a lightweight signal standardization layer plus a smart oncall throttler to reduce false positive paging while preserving high sensitivity to real customer-impact incidents. Scope: 1) Add trace/span hooks at the API gateway and serving runtime to attach consistent routing metadata (model_variant, deployment_tier, customer_tier, inferred_request_type). 2) Implement an ingest normalization stage in the metrics/log pipeline that normalizes latency/error dimensions, enforces tag ontology, and preserves high-cardinality keys for downstream SLO bucketing. 3) Deploy a fast anomaly detector that augments burn-rate alerts with pattern scoring (seasonality-aware z-score + EWMA) and a lightweight classifier to decide paging vs. ticketing. Non-goals: full rework of tracing sampling policy or replacing the observability backend.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All production ingress traces include at least the required tags (model_variant, deployment_tier, customer_tier, request_class) for 99% of requests within one day of rollout. 2) Normalizer emits standardized metric names and labels for the top 25 latency/error metrics across services and routes. 3) Burn-rate alerts must be extended to include anomaly_score and noise_classifier_decision fields. 4) Paging rate for non-customer-impact alerts drops by >=40% in the canary namespace without increasing customer-visible error rate. 5) Runbook updated and verified with a simulated incident drill.
design_notes: Tracing hooks: add middleware in api-gateway (Go) and serving-runtime (C++/Rust) that writes a small envelope into the trace context: {origin, model_variant, route_key, sampling_bucket}. We will prefer tag propagation via B3/traceparent + custom baggage keys. Sampling strategy: keep existing adaptive sampler but ensure 100% header propagation for sampled traces. Ingest normalizer: a Flink-based lightweight job (or kstream) that receives kafka topics from metrics and logs, applies mapping rules (name aliases, histogram conversions), and enriches with customer mapping from tenants service. SLO computation: add a windowed aggregation service that computes per-bucket SLOs (5m, 1h, 6h) and emits burn-rate metrics. Anomaly detector: two-stage pipeline — cheap statistical detector (seasonal z-score) to catch sudden deltas, and a pretrained logistic classifier that ingests short history features (rate of change, tag entropy, infra maintenance flag) to predict whether to page. Throttler policy: if classifier predicts 'low-confidence-customer-impact' and anomaly_score < 0.8, suppress paging and create a lower-priority ticket automatically. Observability UX: new dashboard panels for per-model SLOs and a timeline of suppressed vs paged alerts.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2w): Instrument tracing hooks at api-gateway and a single serving-runtime pool (canary). Phase 2 (2w): Deploy normalizer to staging topics, add mapping rules for top routes, end-to-end test with synthetic traffic. Phase 3 (3w): Wire SLO windowing service and burn-rate metrics, add anomaly detector in evaluation mode (no suppression). Phase 4 (1w): Enable smart throttler in canary namespace with 24/7 oncall monitoring. Phase 5 (rollout): Gradual expansion by traffic weight with rollback gates.
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for normalizer mappings, integration tests that verify tag propagation and SLO buckets, canary synthetic incidents to validate detector precision/recall. Validation metrics: false suppression rate <5%, detection latency <30s for major regressions, paging reduction >=40% in canary. Create a dedicated chaos job that replays historical incidents and measures decision parity.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary namespace (5% traffic) for 48h with anomaly detector in audit-only mode. 2) If metrics look good, enable throttler for non-critical alerts for 7 days. 3) Increment traffic 25% every 3 days with checkpoints. 4) Full rollout if under suppression thresholds. Rollback knob: emergency feature flag to revert throttler and normalization mappings.
monitoring_and_observability: Dashboard links: https://console.redwood.company/dashboards/model-slo-overview (canary panel), https://console.redwood.company/dashboards/alert-suppression (suppression timeline). Logging: structured logs to datadog with tag normalized=true. Burn-rate traces: include trace_id, anomaly_score, classifier_decision in event payload for postmortem analysis.
runbook_and_playbooks: Add runbook: 'Suppressed Alert Triage' with steps to re-enable paging, how to interpret classifier features, and how to add temporary whitelist rules. Link: https://drive.redwood.company/observability/runbooks/suppressed-alert-triage.md
